key_facts: Futurism spotted a startup called Outlit that pitches businesses on near-constant AI monitoring of individual customers.
Founder Josh Earle told Futurism: 'Every company will soon assign an AI agent to every customer to watch their every move.'
Per Futurism, the agents would scan call logs with company staff and outside sources such as customers' social media posts, building profiles and action plans to keep them buying.
Outlit's website says customer data is secure and anonymized.
Earle told Futurism that nothing it does is illegal.
Gizmodo's piece is critical commentary on the idea.
quote_evidence: "Every company will soon assign an AI agent to every customer to watch their every move," founder Josh Earle told Futurism.
"There's nothing that we're doing that's illegal, so we're within our right to be able to monitor signals," Earle told Futurism.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows a startup selling continuous customer monitoring while public opinion is wary of surveillance.
notes: Futurism's original not read; Gizmodo article is commentary.
title: AI Startup Wants Every Company to Assign You Your Own Personal Stalker
